International treaties are pieces of paper that governments ignore whenever it's convenient. The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969) says they're binding, which is adorable.

Here's how to make a treaty actually work: combine it with [incentive structures](../appendix/incentive-alignment-bonds-paper.qmd) that make following the rules more profitable than breaking them. The treaty provides legal cover. The incentives provide actual enforcement.

## Why Treaties Matter (Sort Of)

### What Treaties Actually Do

Treaties aren't magical. They're legal frameworks that work when someone has an incentive to enforce them. Here's what they provide:

#### Supremacy Clause (US Constitution, Article VI)

"Treaties... shall be the supreme Law of the Land"

- Overrides state law
- Overrides federal law  
- Can only be overruled by Constitution itself
- Courts must enforce them

##### International Law Principle: Pacta Sunt Servanda

"Agreements must be kept"

- Core principle of international law
- Breaking treaties = pariah status
- Trade sanctions follow
- Military alliances crumble

#### The Ratchet Effect

- Easy to sign (executive + simple majority)
- Hard to break (requires international consent)
- Hard to secretly violate (everyone watches)
- Violations trigger penalties (if someone enforces them)

Treaties make it marginally harder to break promises. Whether that matters depends entirely on who's enforcing.

## A 1% treaty Structure

### The Core Provisions

#### Article 1: Definitions

- "Military spending" = All military appropriations
- "Eligible Research" = Pragmatic clinical trials funded by the 1% Treaty Fund.
- "Implementation" = Automatic transfer, no annual approval

Define everything so they can't weasel out later.

##### Article 2: The Obligation

- "Parties shall redirect 1% of military budgets to pragmatic clinical trials"
- "Transfers shall be automatic and irrevocable"
- "Percentages may only increase, never decrease"
- "Withdrawal requires unanimous consent of all parties"

Designed as a one-way ratchet. Works if people follow it.

###### Article 3: Enforcement

- Loss of IAB benefits for non-compliant politicians
- Public reporting of all violations
- Exclusion from treaty fund advantages
- Private right of action for citizens

The treaty gives everyone standing to enforce. The real enforcement is exclusion from the profitable system.

###### Article 4: Expansion

- Automatic increase if 50% of parties increase
- New members must match highest percentage
- Success metrics trigger percentage reviews
- Public referendum can force increases

Mechanisms that could create pressure for growth, if the incentives align.

### Key Provisions

#### The Prisoner's Dilemma Solver

- Simultaneous reduction = no military disadvantage
- Verification through public budgets
- Relative power unchanged
- Absolute spending decreased

This solves the coordination problem. Whether anyone actually coordinates depends on the incentives.

#### The Political Cover

- "Supporting the troops" (their healthcare)
- "National security" (pandemic preparedness)
- "Economic growth" (healthier workforce)
- "International cooperation" (looks good)

Politicians can claim victory.

#### The Escape Clause That Isn't

- "Emergency suspension for declared war"
- But: Must be actual declared war (none since 1945)
- And: Only for attacked party
- And: Automatically reinstates after
- And: False claims result in permanent IAB exclusion

Looks flexible, actually rigid.

## Enforcement (The Hard Part)

Treaties don't enforce themselves. Here's what actually makes countries comply:

### Traditional Mechanisms (Weak)

#### Public Transparency

- Annual compliance report cards
- Real-time violation tracking
- Media coverage of non-compliance
- NGO monitoring and reporting

Transparency creates political costs. But the real cost is loss of IAB benefits.

#### Economic Consequences

- Loss of IAB-funded political advantages
- Opponents gain exclusive access to bond benefits
- Political isolation as other leaders gain IAB support
- Reduced competitiveness in elections

Money talks in every language. Especially campaign money.

#### Legal Standing

- International Court of Justice jurisdiction (for what it's worth)
- Domestic court enforcement (where applicable)
- Private arbitration options
- Individual lawsuits allowed

Multiple venues to establish violations. The real consequence is losing IAB access.

### The Smart Contract Approach

#### Blockchain Treaty Execution

- Treaty terms in smart contracts
- Automatic fund transfers
- Cryptographic verification
- Immutable violation record

This makes violations harder to hide. Doesn't make anyone care.

#### The Oracle Problem

- Multiple data sources confirm budgets
- AI monitors compliance
- Satellite imagery verifies military spending
- Public records provide transparency

Transparency is useful. Enforcement still requires someone with an incentive to act on it.

### What Actually Works (Incentives)

None of the above mechanisms matter unless someone has an incentive to enforce them. That's where [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../appendix/incentive-alignment-bonds-paper.qmd) come in.

The bonds make it profitable for politicians to comply with the treaty:

- **Comply** → get IAB campaign funding, post-office board positions, political advantages
- **Vote against** → your opponents get those benefits, you don't, you lose elections
- **Try to cheat** → lose access to entire IAB system, political opponents gain massive funding advantage

**The "penalty" is exclusion, not punishment:**

- No need for enforcement bodies with military power
- No need for magical "automatic penalties"
- Just: follow the rules or get shut out of the profitable system
- Your opponents will gladly take the IAB money you forfeited

Public choice theory in action. Politicians don't follow treaties because they're noble. They follow treaties when following them makes them richer and more powerful than breaking them. The enforcement is built into the incentive structure itself.

## Avoiding the Pitfalls

### Common Treaty Killers

#### Reservation Games

- Countries sign but add exceptions
- Solution: No reservations permitted
- All or nothing commitment
- Take it or leave it

#### Ratification Delays

- Sign but never ratify
- Solution: Provisional application
- Takes effect on signature
- Ratification just formalizes

#### Creative Accounting

- Reclassify military as non-military
- Solution: Total budget percentage
- Can't hide spending
- AI detects classification games

#### Parliamentary Obstacles

- Legislature refuses implementation
- Solution: Self-executing treaty
- No implementing legislation needed
- Direct effect in domestic law

## The Expansion Framework

### From 1% to More

If the 1% model works, people will want to expand it. Here's how that could happen:

#### Year 1-2: Proof of Concept

- 1% redirected (if compliance mechanisms work)
- First results from clinical trials
- Public sees what's possible
- Some politicians look for credit

##### Year 3-5: Possible Expansion

- If successful, treaty review triggers
- Public pressure might build
- Some countries might increase to 2-5%
- Early political advantages accrue to supporters

###### Year 5-10: If Momentum Continues

- Compliance could become standard
- Progressive countries might reach 10%
- Military contractors might pivot to biotech
- Profit incentives could shift

###### Long Term: Optimistic Scenario

- If every step works as planned
- If incentives stay aligned
- If public support grows
- Military spending could become politically toxic

That's the hope, anyway. Lots of "ifs."

## The Model Treaty Text

### Preamble

"Recognizing that humanity spends 40 times more on killing than curing,

Acknowledging that 150,000 people die daily from preventable diseases,

Determined to redirect resources from death to life,

Convinced that security comes from health, not weapons,

Have agreed as follows..."

### Operative Clauses

**Article 1:** Parties shall redirect 1% of military spending to a 1% Treaty Fund for allocation to pragmatic clinical trials.

**Article 2:** Transfers shall be automatic, immediate, and irrevocable

**Article 3:** Percentages may increase but never decrease

**Article 4:** Compliance shall be verified by blockchain and AI

**Article 5:** Non-compliant parties lose access to IAB benefits and treaty fund advantages

**Article 6:** Success metrics trigger mandatory percentage reviews

**Article 7:** Citizens have standing to enforce via domestic courts

**Article 8:** Withdrawal requires unanimous consent plus 10-year notice

**Article 9:** This treaty supersedes all conflicting domestic law

**Article 10:** Entry into force upon signature by two states

Simple and clear. Escapable if you're willing to pay the price.

## How This Actually Works

A 1% treaty provides legal structure for [incentive alignment bonds](../appendix/incentive-alignment-bonds-paper.qmd) to operate. The treaty alone doesn't enforce anything. The bonds make compliance profitable for politicians.

The treaty says "redirect 1% of military budgets." The bonds make politicians who vote for it rich and popular. The bonds make politicians who vote against it unemployed. That's how enforcement works in a world run by self-interested humans.

**The enforcement mechanism is exclusion, not punishment:**

- Countries that comply: their politicians get IAB funding and advantages
- Countries that don't: their politicians' opponents get those benefits instead
- No need for UN peacekeepers or international enforcement bodies
- Just political competition for access to a profitable system

Think of it like credit cards: Visa doesn't send soldiers to your house if you don't pay. Your credit score tanks and no one lends to you anymore. The punishment IS exclusion from the system.

Public choice theory says politicians respond to incentives, not laws. The treaty provides the framework. The bonds provide the incentives. Together they might actually work.

If it works at 1%, people will see results. If people see results, they'll want more. That's not legally inevitable. That's just how humans react when something actually helps them instead of killing them.
